required_plan: A customer-owned Cloudflare account with Workers Paid, D1, R2, Queues, Cron Triggers, and the required Email Service access.

atomic_store.notes: D1 transactions atomically persist provider-neutral delivery state and the deterministic outbox.

recipient_ledger.notes: D1 stores canonical messages, recipients, attempts, provider events, suppressions, and outbox items.

payload_store.notes: Private R2 stores payload objects referenced by the D1 delivery authority.

queue_wakeup.notes: Cloudflare Queues delivers deterministic at-least-once jobs to the Worker and a dedicated dead-letter queue.

scheduler_wakeup.notes: Queue delay accelerates due work while D1 due times and Cron reconciliation retain the 30-day HayaSend contract.

periodic_reconciliation.notes: A one-minute Cron trigger leases and republishes due D1 outbox rows after a lost queue wake-up.

secret_injection.notes: Wrangler writes the API secret to the customer-owned Worker without retaining it in deployment evidence.

provider_event_ingress.notes: The Worker consumes Email Sending Queue events after the operator creates the documented per-domain event subscription.

webhook_egress.notes: The current Cloudflare proof runtime does not expose the full webhook surface.

backup_restore.notes: Exact-main hosted evidence exports D1, copies retained R2 objects with metadata and digests, restores both into an isolated namespace, verifies relational and payload integrity, recovers due work exactly once without an external send, and removes every named proof resource.

safe_deploy.notes: Plan-first deployment binds deterministic D1, R2, Queue, and Worker resources to an explicitly confirmed account.

doctor.notes: Doctor verifies deployment identity, health, capability digests, authenticated API behavior, and event-subscription truth.

upgrade.notes: Additive D1 migrations and immutable Worker versions support reviewed upgrades.

rollback.notes: Rollback targets a reviewed immutable Worker version while preserving D1 and R2 state.

cleanup.notes: Cleanup removes the event subscription and deterministic Worker, R2, Queue, and D1 resources with fail-closed absence checks.

sources.title: Exact-main isolated D1 and R2 restore evidence

limitations: Production readiness remains false until issue #122 proves a terminal provider event and controlled mailbox receipt.
Webhook delivery, hosted templates, domain management, and inbound email are outside the current proof runtime.
